Path('tmp/pdfs/manuscript.txt').write_text('\\n\\n'.join(f'=== PAGE {i+1} ===\\n'+p.extract_text() for i,p in enumerate(r.pages)))

folder=Path('tmp/pdfs')

folder.rmdir()
print('Removed temporary extraction and rendering files.')
PY"

strengths: The method addresses an important computer vision problem: distilling high-resolution datasets without expensive bi-level optimization. Combining class-specific feature representatives with weighted per-class BatchNorm regularization provides a practical approach to preserving intra-class variation.

The reported improvements are substantial across several settings. At 50 IPC, WMDD achieves 59.4% on Tiny ImageNet and 57.6% on ImageNet-1K, compared with 48.7% and 53.5% for the strongest listed baselines. Table 2 also provides encouraging transfer results across ResNet and ViT architectures.

The factorial ablation in Table 4 usefully separates the feature objective from BatchNorm regularization. With PCBN fixed, Wasserstein feature matching improves ImageNet-1K accuracy from 36.4% to 38.1%. Layer selection, regularization sensitivity, and sliced Wasserstein experiments provide additional evidence about design choices.

The manuscript provides pseudocode, implementation settings, and a public code link, and credits the underlying optimal transport algorithm, POT library, and datasets. The supplementary visualizations illustrate increased synthetic-image diversity, and the societal-impact discussion appropriately acknowledges propagation of source-data biases.
weaknesses: The novelty of the central objective needs clearer positioning. With squared Euclidean cost, one source distribution, and freely optimized synthetic weights, Eq. (5) reduces exactly to minimizing (1/n) sum_i min_j ||z_i-b_j||²: classical k-means quantization. The manuscript neither discusses this equivalence nor compares k-means feature targets within the same PCBN and relabeling pipeline. This leaves the contribution of the proposed barycenter optimization insufficiently established, although its integration into distillation may still be useful.

A substantial baseline discrepancy undermines confidence in the headline comparisons. On ImageNet-1K at 10 IPC, Table 1 reports SRe2L at 21.3%, whereas the CE-plus-standard-BN configuration in Table 4 reaches 35.9%, close to WMDD's 38.1%. The manuscript does not explain which additional components or training settings account for this difference. Comparisons using matched teachers, relabeling, weighting, and evaluation protocols are needed to establish how much improvement comes from the proposed method.

The metric comparison in Section 5.6 does not isolate the metric from the representation and regularization choices. At one IPC, the squared-Wasserstein representative is simply the class feature mean, making Eq. (12) equivalent to linear-kernel MMD mean matching for a fixed encoder. Consequently, Figure 4's 5.77% versus 0.48% gap cannot establish a metric advantage under otherwise identical conditions. Appendix B's dismissal of characteristic-kernel MMD on quadratic-cost grounds is also incomplete: the real-real kernel term is constant during synthesis and can be omitted from optimization.

The solver specification has consequential ambiguities. Algorithm 2 updates the weights after computing the transport plan, then reuses that plan for the position update, although Eq. (11) assumes its column marginals match the weights used in the denominator. Simplex projection also permits zero weights, making this division undefined. Transport-plan recomputation, zero-mass handling, support initialization, the weight learning rate, and the precise use of weights in FKD need clarification. The stated convergence claim is not established by the algorithm as written.

The efficiency evidence only partially supports the scalability claims. The cross-method timing comparison uses ImageNette at one IPC, where feature quantization reduces to computing a mean. Table 5 adds useful Tiny ImageNet timings, but ImageNet-scale measurements separating teacher training, feature extraction, transport, synthesis, and relabeling costs are missing. These would clarify the practical cost of the method at the budgets where its strongest results occur.
